# RISC-V Debug Module Wrapper — Behavioral Specification

## Overview

The module implements a RISC-V debug system according to the RISC-V Debug Specification version 0.13. It provides external debug access over JTAG, run-control of one or more harts, debug-memory access for execution-based debug, and system-bus access through a dedicated master interface. The module also provides local control/status registers, alert reporting, and hardware debug-enable gating controlled by the system lifecycle.

The module shall operate with a single clock and an asynchronous active-low reset. It shall not be reset by the non-debug module reset request that it generates.

## Configuration

- The number of harts must be greater than zero.
- All configured harts shall have contiguous hart IDs and shall be selectable by the debugger.
- The JTAG IDCODE value shall be configurable and shall be returned when the JTAG TAP selects the IDCODE instruction.
- Alert synchronization behavior shall be configurable per alert output.

## JTAG Debug Transport

The module shall provide a JTAG interface conforming to IEEE 1149.1 and to the RISC-V Debug Transport Module specification. The JTAG interface includes a test clock, test mode select, optional test reset, test data input, test data output, and an output-enable indication.

The JTAG TAP shall support the standard instructions required by the RISC-V Debug specification, including IDCODE, BYPASS, and DMI access. The returned IDCODE shall be the configured value.

The module shall translate JTAG DMI operations into Debug Module Interface (DMI) read and write transactions. The DMI shall provide access to the debug module register set. DMI operations must be accepted only when the hardware debug enable is in the enabled state. When DMI access is disabled, incoming DMI request/response activity shall be suppressed and no debug module register access shall be performed.

## Debug Module Control and Run Control

The module shall implement the RISC-V Debug Module register set and shall report specification version 0.13.

The module shall support selection of one hart at a time. Hart array mask operations are not supported. When a halt is requested for the selected hart, the module shall assert the corresponding debug request output to that hart. When a resume is requested, the module shall release the halt request and track the hart’s resume acknowledgement.

The module shall track and report the state of each hart:

- halted
- running
- unavailable
- resumed
- nonexistent, where applicable

These states shall be reflected in the debug module status and halt summary registers accessible through DMI.

The module shall report a hart as unavailable when the corresponding availability input is asserted. This information shall be visible to the debugger through the status registers.

The module shall implement abstract commands using the program buffer. It shall provide command-busy and command-error status. It shall make the program buffer and abstract data registers accessible through the debug memory address space.

Halt-on-reset is not supported. Writes requesting halt-on-reset shall have no effect, and the capability shall be reported as unsupported.

Authentication is not supported. The module shall report the debugger as authenticated and not busy.

Hardware triggers are not supported. Trigger-related accesses shall read as zero.

## Reset and Debug Active Outputs

The module shall provide a non-debug module reset output. This output shall be asserted when the debugger requests a non-debug module reset through the debug module control register and the reset request is enabled by the hardware debug-enable gating. The output shall remain asserted while the reset request is active and shall be deasserted when the request is cleared or when reset request gating is disabled.

The module shall provide a debug-active output. This output shall indicate that the debug module has been activated by the debugger. It shall be asserted when the debug module is active and deasserted when it is not active. The system may use this output to prevent powering down harts or bus-attached peripherals that may be accessed by the debugger.

## Debug Memory Interface

The module shall provide a bus slave interface that exposes the debug memory. The debug memory includes the debug ROM, program buffer, abstract command/data area, and control/status locations used for execution-based debug.

The debug memory shall be accessible for both read and write operations as appropriate for each region:

- The debug ROM shall be read-only.
- The program buffer shall be writable by the debugger.
- The abstract data and command locations shall be writable and readable as specified by the RISC-V Debug specification.

Debug memory accesses shall be performed at word granularity. Sub-word byte enables are not supported; all byte enables are treated as asserted.

The debug memory bus shall be gated by the hardware debug-enable state. When the debug-memory enable is not active, the module shall not accept new accesses to the debug memory. When the enable is active, accesses shall be serviced normally.

Instruction fetch from the debug memory shall be permitted only when the instruction-fetch enable is active. If instruction fetch is disabled, instruction accesses to the debug memory shall not be enabled, while data accesses may still proceed if the debug-memory enable is active.

## System Bus Access

The module shall provide a bus master interface for System Bus Access (SBA). Through the DMI-accessible SBA registers, the debugger shall be able to read and write arbitrary system bus addresses.

The SBA functionality shall implement the behavior required by the RISC-V Debug specification, including:

- address and data registers
- read and write operations
- access width control
- address auto-increment
- read-on-address
- read-on-data
- busy and error status reporting

SBA operations shall not generate requests when the SBA enable is not active. When SBA is disabled, the bus master interface shall be held inactive and SBA responses shall be ignored.

The SBA bus interface shall not expect error responses from system bus targets. Error status for SBA operations shall be reported through the SBA control/status register as defined by the RISC-V Debug specification.

## Hardware Debug Enable Gating

The module shall accept a hardware debug-enable input from the system lifecycle controller. This input must be synchronized within the module before use.

The following debug functions shall be enabled only when the hardware debug-enable is in the enabled state:

- DMI access from JTAG
- debug memory access
- instruction fetch from debug memory
- system bus access
- debug request outputs
- non-debug module reset request output

When the hardware debug-enable is not enabled, all of the above functions shall be held inactive. The module’s local control/status bus, alerts, and JTAG TAP behavior may remain available independently of this gating.

## Scan Mode

When scan mode is enabled, the JTAG clock and reset inputs shall be overridden by the system clock and scan reset inputs. This allows the JTAG and DMI logic to operate during scan-based testing. In normal mode, the JTAG clock and reset shall be taken from the external JTAG interface.

The module shall operate correctly in both normal and scan modes.

## Local Control/Status Bus

The module shall provide an additional bus slave interface for local module registers. This interface shall allow access to module-level control and status information, including an alert test control.

The local control/status interface shall respond to bus transactions according to the TL-UL protocol and shall report integrity errors as described below.

## Alerts

The module shall generate an alert when an integrity error is detected on a bus slave interface or in the associated register/memory logic. This includes the local control/status slave and the debug memory slave.

The alert output shall be asserted through a fatal alert sender. The sender shall support asynchronous alert synchronization according to configuration and shall allow an alert to be triggered for testing via the local control/status register.

If the alert test bit is set, the module shall assert the alert as a test indication. The alert output shall be deasserted when the test bit is cleared and no integrity error is present.

## Compliance Notes

The module shall be compliant with RISC-V Debug Specification 0.13. Optional features that are not implemented shall read as disabled or unsupported in the relevant status fields. The module shall not insert an implicit ebreak after the program buffer. Configuration string pointer support shall be reported as unavailable.
